title: Lifting a compactification to its base with separated finite-type middle scheme
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme (quasi-compact as a topological space, with quasi-compact intersection of any two quasi-compact opens). Let $a_X:X\to S$ and $a_Y:Y\to S$ be schemes over $S$, and let $f:X\to Y$ satisfy $a_Y\circ f=a_X$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Assume $a_Y$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let
$$
c=(X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y)
$$
be any compactification of the underlying scheme morphism $f$ [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], so $p\circ i=f$, $i$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ is proper.

There is a unique structure morphism $a_Z:Z\to S$ making both $i$ and $p$ morphisms over $S$; it is $a_Z=a_Y\circ p$. For this structure, $a_Z$ is separated and of finite type, and $Z$ is quasi-compact as a scheme. The factorization $p\circ i=f$ therefore holds in $\mathit{Sch}/S$, with the same underlying open immersion and proper morphism. No finite-type or separatedness assumption on $a_X$ is required, and no existence or choice of $c$ is asserted.

proof.text: Define $a_Z=a_Y\circ p$. By the definition of an $S$-morphism, $p$ is over $S$ because $a_Y\circ p=a_Z$. Associativity and the two assumed commutativities give $a_Z\circ i=a_Y\circ(p\circ i)=a_Y\circ f=a_X$, so $i$ is over $S$ as well. Conversely, any $b:Z\to S$ for which $p$ is over $S$ must satisfy $b=a_Y\circ p=a_Z$; thus the structure morphism is unique. In the category $\mathit{Sch}/S$ the two arrows have the original underlying maps $i,p$, and their composite equals $f$ because its underlying map is $p\circ i=f$; equality of $S$-morphisms is equality of their underlying morphisms. Their open-immersion and properness properties are precisely those supplied by the given compactification.

source.place: Statement paragraph 3: the middle scheme and both maps over the base; the explicit associativity and uniqueness argument. Stacks Tag 01JX, schemes-definition-scheme-over, gives the definitions.

proof.text: The properness of $p$ implies, by the definition of proper, that $p$ is separated and of finite type. These are the two properties of $p$ needed below; no geometric property of $a_X$ is used.

Apply the separated-composition assertion (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] to $p:Z\to Y$ and $a_Y:Y\to S$. Its first separatedness hypothesis is step 2, and its second is a hypothesis of this item. The conclusion is that $a_Y\circ p=a_Z$ is separated.

Apply clause (1) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] to $p:Z\to Y$ and $a_Y:Y\to S$. Both morphisms are of finite type, respectively by step 2 and by hypothesis. Hence their composite $a_Z$ is of finite type.

Finite type includes quasi-compactness of the morphism, so step 4 implies that $a_Z$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply clause (2), quasi-compact case, of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] with $U=Z$, $T=S$, and morphism $a_Z$. Its base quasi-compactness hypothesis is part of the stated qcqs hypothesis on $S$. Thus $Z$ is quasi-compact as a scheme. Together with steps 1, 3 and 4 this proves every assertion for the given $c$. Neither an existence theorem for compactifications nor a choice of one has been used.

Uniqueness of a_Z is forced by p being over S, and quasi-compactness of Z needs S quasi-compact (counterexample: an infinite disjoint union of Spec of a field). Step 1 (elementary): the S-morphism definition gives a_Z=a_Y∘p, both i and p are over S, and a_Z is unique. Step 4: clause (1) of lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change (Stacks 01T3). Step 5: finite type includes quasi-compact, then clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence with U=Z, T=S (Stacks 01K4 checked at schemes.tex:3584). Off-unit citations are only Mathlib leaves and definitions, so no tool_uses are needed. There is no SGA, no Nagata existence or choice, and no cycle. Edge cases checked: X=∅, Z=∅, p=id, and proper components of Z away from X. The item is not in a dropped list and has no re-split note.
